aliases: LangChain vs LangGraph vs Deep Agents
nodes.boundary_definition: A choice model for the relative abstraction and control offered by the LangChain framework, LangGraph runtime, and Deep Agents harness, including the create_agent and deepagents entry points.
nodes.purpose: Prevents selecting an abstraction without understanding its control and convenience tradeoff.

nodes.boundary_definition: The inputs, tool calls, messages, and state transitions that let an agent observe, act, and continue a task.
nodes.purpose: Makes agent behavior traceable instead of treating it as a single prompt.

nodes.boundary_definition: Control points that shape context, intercept execution, connect external tools, load agent instructions or skills, sandbox work, or require human approval.
nodes.purpose: Controls long conversations, risky actions, tool access, and changing runtime context.

nodes.boundary_definition: Recording agent runs, organizing representative inputs and expected evidence, adding cases, and comparing experiments for repeatable evaluation.
nodes.purpose: Turns opaque agent behavior into inspectable test evidence without confusing a trace with a quality judgment.

nodes.boundary_definition: Choosing and calibrating an evaluation method based on available ground truth, quality dimensions, online or offline context, cost, and failure tolerance.
nodes.purpose: Avoids treating one evaluator as a universal measure of agent quality.

nodes.boundary_definition: The runtime boundary that hosts an agent, names deployment primitives, preserves thread or assistant state, handles secrets and durable storage, serves across regions where needed, and authenticates or authorizes callers.
nodes.purpose: Makes deployment behavior, resilience, and tenant boundaries explicit.

nodes.boundary_definition: Operational observations that reveal whether an agent is affordable, responsive, correct enough, reliable, safe, and producing acceptable user experience; includes traces grouped into threads, Insights, Online Evals, and alerts.
nodes.purpose: Connects signals to interventions rather than dashboards for their own sake.

nodes.boundary_definition: An evidence loop that treats building, testing, deploying, and monitoring as connected lifecycle activities.
nodes.purpose: Maps certification domains to a coherent real-world engineering workflow.

nodes.boundary_definition: Build and explain an agent with appropriate abstractions, tools, state, context, and control flow.
nodes.purpose: Creates a working agent model and artifact.

nodes.boundary_definition: Use traces, datasets, experiments, and evaluators to test an agent.
nodes.purpose: Produces direct evidence about behavior and failure.

nodes.boundary_definition: Deploy an agent with explicit state and authentication decisions.
nodes.purpose: Moves from local prototype to controlled runtime.

nodes.boundary_definition: Use operational signals to diagnose and improve an agent in production.
nodes.purpose: Closes the lifecycle with evidence-driven operation.

clusters.name: Build agents
clusters.purpose: Choose abstractions and make agent behavior explicit.

clusters.name: Deploy agents
clusters.purpose: Operate a controlled runtime with state and auth.

clusters.name: Monitor agents
clusters.purpose: Use production signals to improve the system.

clusters.name: Agent lifecycle
clusters.purpose: Connect the four certification domains into one loop.
